advisory.summary: hawkBit's DDI controller API served a software module's artifacts to any authenticated device in the tenant, without checking the module was assigned to that device: the artifact download when the request carried a Range header, and the artifact listing on every request.
note: GHSA-92r3-p8c2-3fpx, reported by Santoshkumarpuppala.
DdiRootController on 1.0.3 served a software module's artifacts by module
id, with the device's own controllerId and token, and no check that the
module was assigned to that device. Two paths reached another device's
firmware: the download GET .../softwaremodules/{smId}/artifacts/{fileName},
whose only assignment check ran inside logDownload, which ran only when
the request had no Range header; and the listing GET
.../softwaremodules/{smId}/artifacts, which had no check at all.
1.0.4 makes the download check unconditional (commit 6cb34fd,
getActionForDownloadByTargetAndSoftwareModule before streaming) and adds
the same check to the listing (commit 914b8b4); a module not assigned to
the caller answers 404 (SoftwareModuleNotAssignedToTargetException).
Measured on both tags before this was written. Device B, with its own
controllerId and token, naming device A's module: the ranged download
(Range: bytes=0-) is 206 with device A's firmware bytes, which carry the
marker, on 1.0.3 and 404 on 1.0.4; the listing is 200 with the marker
filename on 1.0.3 and 404 on 1.0.4. Without a Range header the download
was already 404 on 1.0.3, which is why the ranged request is the one
checked.
Device A's module holds two artifacts: one whose filename is the marker,
for the listing, and one with a plain filename whose bytes carry the
marker, for the download, so no marker is ever in a request.
The owner's marker_probe -- device A listing its own module -- is 200 with
the marker on both builds. DDI paths the resource by the caller's own
controllerId, so the owner cannot share the attacker's path in one check;
the attacker paths' second identity is an unauthenticated caller, 401 on
both builds. The third check is device B listing its OWN assigned module,
200 on both, so device B's token is live and the patched 404s are the fix,
not a dead credential; a fabricated TargetToken gets 401 on both.
Devices authenticate with their own per-target security token
(Authorization: TargetToken <token>), enabled by the provisioner. The
images are linux/amd64 only and run emulated on arm64 hosts.

checks.name: A device must not list another device's module artifact metadata
A device must not download another device's firmware artifact (ranged request)
A device must still list the artifacts of a module assigned to it
